title: CFT representation of interacting bulk gauge fields in AdS

reference.volume-title: Proceedings of the 4th Canadian Conference on General Relativity and Relativistic Astrophysics
reference.author: K. V. Kuchar

items.abstract: <jats:p>We introduce PCW geometry, a five-dimensional bulk–boundary framework in which an infinite three-dimensional observational representation is encoded by a finite or conformally compact five-dimensional bulk BPCW 5 and its four-dimensional surface-record manifold MPCW 4 The geometric foundation is the identification MPCW 4 =∂confBPCW 5 . =D◦ R(TS2), so that a surface record is locally coordinatized by (ϑ,φ,α,ρ), where (ϑ,φ) specify a celestial direction and (α,ρ) specify the finite surface-impact record. Adding the inward conformal depth coordinate z gives BPCW 5 =[0,z∗) ×MPCW 4 . We construct a covariant action SPCW = SPCW[g,σ,Q,Φ], where gAB is the bulk metric, σ is the PCW scale/warp mode, QAB is a transverse-traceless trace-free shape mode, and Φ denotes matter and quantum fields. Its Euler–Lagrange equations yield the PCW Einstein equation, the scale-mode equation, the shape-mode equation, and the matter-field equation. The perturbative shape sector is Fierz–Pauli tuned and transverse-traceless, with QAA = 0, ∇AQAB = 0, and m2 Q ≥ m2 BF,TT; in the conservative AdS5 branch we impose m2 QL2 ≥ 0. The scale mode obeys the scalar BF condition m2 σ,effL2 ≥ −4. Under these hypotheses the quadratic fluctuation sector is ghost-free and spectrally stable. We prove that any four-dimensional Ricci-flat Lorentzian metric γµν admits the PCW lift ds2 5 = L2 z2 (dz2 +γµνdyµdyν), which satisfies RAB = −(4/L2)gAB. Consequently Schwarzschild and Kerr are PCW vacuum branches. Their non-extremal horizons have Rindler normal compactifications: for Schwarzschild z =z0e−ct/(2rs), and for Kerr z = z0e−κHτ. Hence r → rH is equivalent to z → 0, and the horizon record surface is a PCW conformal boundary. The homogeneous and isotropic cosmological branch has the FLRW form ds2 4 = −c2dt2+a2(t)dΣ2 k. A PCW Noether charge gives EPCW 5D = constant. With EPCW 5D =Eapp Λ +Eapp m +EPCW one obtains the exact compensation law dEPCW warp dt =−d dt (Eapp warp , Λ +Eapp m ). Thus apparent three-dimensional dark-energy growth is compatible with exact five-dimensional PCW energy conservation. Finally, the bulk–boundary information map Π∞ : C(BPCW 5 ) → C(MPCW 4 ) is formulated sec torwise for particles, fields, and quantum states. Under the stated reconstruction and unitarity hypotheses, Π∞ is bijective. In the minimal AdS5 branch this yields ZAdS5 [Φ|∂AdS5 = J] = ZCFT4 [J], so AdS5/CFT4 is obtained as a PCW theorem. The same information identity resolves the black-hole information problem in the PCW setting and predicts IEL > 0 for non-factorized unitary evaporation. The raw-likelihood implementation described here is stated to survive all included data blocks, and the compressed cross-check gives ηH = 0.08754±0.01821, ∆χ2 ≃ 23.12, and lnKPCW/std ≃ 9.39 for the scale sector, while the current compressed black-hole sector remains consistent with qµν = 0.</jats:p>
title: PCW GEOMETRY, BULK–BOUNDARY INFORMATION EQUIVALENCE, AND OBSERVATIONAL TESTS: A FIVE-DIMENSIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR ADS/CFT, BLACK-HOLE INFORMATION, AND COSMOLOGICAL ENERGY CONSERVATION
